newsitem.title: USA: Clark PUD, BPA to sell lower-cost power to SEH.
newsitem.headline: Clark PUD, BPA to sell lower-cost power to SEH.

text.p: Clark Public Utilities District announced Wednesday an agreement to re-sell power from the Bonneville Power Administration to SEH America of Vancouver, Wash., an industrial firm within the utility's service territory.

SEH had shopped around for a supplier to replace Bonneville, but was able to cut a deal for power at near 2.3 cents per kilowatt hour (KWh), compared with 2.7 cents under its previous contract, Clark said.
The rate includes Clark's 0.23 cent per KWh charge for transmission service, said the utility's spokesman Mick Shutt.
The volume of the deal is initially around 18 MW, but is expected to rise since SEH, a maker of crystals for computers, plans to expand, he said.
The new power contract has a term of 18 months, Shutt added.
